thread:
Sam: quick heads-up / scheduled maintenance for eu-west1 GPU pool tonight 23:30-01:00 UTC. scope: NIC microcode + NVMe remount checks + KV-cache reseed. small cohorts, want low customer impact.
Priya: ack. what's the cohort size and expected cadence?
Sam: canary = 1 rack (~4 GPUs). cohorts of 4 racks, 12m cadence to allow NVMe remount + warm KV.
Diego: NVMe remounts have been flaky after soft-reboot on some blades. plan to use mount options and systemd delay to avoid race with udev.
Maya: network note  NIC flash will drop link briefly. we'll pre-pop ARP and run `bridge fdb flush` on the leaf after each node comes up. expect ~45-90s flap.
Sam: runbook steps: 1) cordon node 2) drain pods (grace 90s) 3) run nvme remount workaround 4) soft reboot 5) kv-warm seed 6) uncordon. rollback: uncordon + reprovision replacement if node fails mount.
Priya: paste drain and nvme commands?
Sam: drain: ```bash
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=90
```
Sam: nvme remount workaround: ```bash
systemctl stop kubelet
for dev in /dev/nvme?n*; do umount $dev || true; rm -f /run/mount/$dev; mount -o nouuid $dev /mnt/local || true; done
systemctl start kubelet
```
Diego: we'll also add a short `udevadm settle` before kubelet start to reduce races.
Maya: monitoring: watch `inference-latency-p95`, `queue-depth`, `kv-cache-hit`, `node-disk-errors`. alert triggers: latency +150ms, queue >800, kv-hit <60%, disk-errors >0.5/min.
Sam: customer comms: only reserved Dedicated customers get calendar invite. Hosted API gets banner and status page post. Support notified.
Priya: cost team: any extra GPU minutes expected?
Sam: minimal if cohorts are small; estimate 3-5% warm backfill usage during window. reserved pools will be used first.
heartbeat-bot: Maintenance notice queued for eu-west1-gpu-pool. Canary scheduled 23:35 UTC. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/eu-west1-gpu-nvme
Diego: starting canary at 23:35. I'll watch disk remount logs and system journal.
Sam: canary results at 23:43: NVMe remount workaround succeeded, p95 +30ms, kv-hit 78%. proceeding to cohort A at 23:55.
Maya: cohort A started; pre-pop ARP done. saw brief 60s flap on rack-3b, no downstream packet loss.
Priya: monitoring green so far, queue stable.
Diego: cohort B encountered a node with stale fstab entry; mount failed and pods entered CrashLoopBackOff.
Sam: pausing rollout. attempting quick fix: correct fstab on node, remount and restart kubelet. if that fails, spin replacement from reserved pool.
Priya: opened incident INC-2026-046: nvme-mount-failure-during-maint. oncall taking lead.
Maya: network unaffected. initiating `bridge fdb flush` post-recover to clear stale MACs.
Diego: patch applied to problematic node; remount succeeded, kubelet restarted, pods recovered.
Sam: cohort B recovery complete. adjusting cadence: increase cooldown to 20m and reduce cohort size to 3 racks to be safe.
Priya: will inform support and update console banner. also will capture cost delta after final.
heartbeat-bot: Maintenance paused at 00:28 UTC for verification. Resume planned 00:50 UTC if green.
Sam: thanks team. follow-ups: add fstab validation to preflight checks and add `udevadm settle` step to runbook. I'll post the post-run notes tomorrow.
Diego: noted. I'll add a small script to validate mountpoints before drain.
Maya: standing by on network watch channel. ping me before each cohort. :thumbsup:
Priya: +1. joining the watch call at 00:45 UTC.
Sam: final: great work. will file short postmortem if incident impact >1h or customer-facing.
